commemorations.local: Vigil of St. Andrew the Apostle

verses.text: Vísio Isaíæ fílii Amos, quam vidit super Judam et Jerúsalem, in diébus Ozíæ, Jóatham, Achaz, et Ezechíæ, regum Juda.
Audíte, cæli, et áuribus pércipe, terra, quóniam Dóminus locútus est: Fílios enutrívi, et exaltávi: ipsi autem sprevérunt me.
Cognóvit bos possessórem suum, et ásinus præsépe dómini sui: Israël autem me non cognóvit, et pópulus meus non intelléxit.

responsory.text: Aspíciens a longe, ecce vídeo Dei poténtiam veniéntem, et nébulam totam terram tegéntem.
responsory.repeat: Ite óbviam ei, et dícite: * Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse, * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

responsory.text: Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum, simul in unum dives et pauper. Ite óbviam ei, et dícite.
Qui regis Israël, inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph. Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse.
Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut salvos fácias nos. * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

parts.title: Lesson from the book of Isaias

verses.text: The vision of Isaias the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Juda and Jerusalem in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda
Hear, O ye heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord hath spoken. I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me.
The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel hath not known me, and my people hath not understood.

responsory.text: I look from afar, and behold I see the Power of God, coming like as a cloud to cover the land with the hosts of his People:
responsory.repeat: Go ye out to meet him and say: * Tell us if thou art he, * That shalt reign over God's people Israel.

responsory.text: All ye that dwell in the world, all ye children of men, high and low, rich and poor, one with another. Go ye out to meet him and say.
Hear, O thou Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep. Tell us if thou art he.
Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut salvos fácias nos. * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

verses.text: Væ genti peccatríci, pópulo gravi iniquitáte, sémini nequam, fíliis scelerátis: dereliquérunt Dóminum, blasphemavérunt Sanctum Israël, abalienáti sunt retrórsum.
Super quo percútiam vos ultra, addéntes prævaricatiónem? omne caput lánguidum, et omne cor mærens.
A planta pedis usque ad vérticem non est in eo sánitas: vulnus, et livor, et plaga tumens non est circumligáta, nec curáta medicámine, neque fota óleo.

responsory.text: Aspiciébam in visu noctis, et ecce in núbibus cæli Fílius hóminis veniébat: et datum est ei regnum, et honor:
responsory.repeat: Et omnis pópulus, tribus, et linguæ sérvient ei.

responsory.text: Potéstas ejus, potéstas ætérna, quæ non auferétur: et regnum ejus, quod non corrumpétur.
Et omnis pópulus, tribus, et linguæ sérvient ei.

verses.text: Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a wicked seed, ungracious children: they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backwards.
For what shall I strike you any more, you that increase transgression? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart is sad.
From the sole of the foot unto the top of the head, there is no soundness therein: wounds and bruises and swelling sores: they are not bound up, nor dressed, nor fomented with oil.

responsory.text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and there was given Him a Kingdom, and glory;
responsory.repeat: And all people, nations, and languages shall serve Him.

responsory.text: His dominion is an everlasting dominion which shall not pass away, and His Kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
And all people, nations, and languages shall serve Him.

verses.text: Terra vestra desérta, civitátes vestræ succénsæ igni: regiónem vestram coram vobis aliéni dévorant, et desolábitur sicut in vastitáte hostíli.
Et derelinquétur fília Sion ut umbráculum in vínea, et sicut tugúrium in cucumerário, et sicut cívitas quæ vastátur.
Nisi Dóminus exercítuum reliquísset nobis semen, quasi Sódoma fuissémus, et quasi Gomórrha símiles essémus.

responsory.text: Missus est Gábriel Angelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Joseph, núntians ei verbum; et expavéscit Virgo de lúmine: ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Dóminum:
responsory.repeat: Ecce concípies, et páries, et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.

responsory.text: Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris ejus, et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum.
Ecce concípies, et páries, et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.

verses.text: Your land is desolate, your cities are burnt with fire: your country strangers devour before your face, and it shall be desolate as when wasted by enemies.
And the daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard, and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, and as a city that is laid waste.
Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom, and we should have been like to Gomorrha.

responsory.text: The Angel Gabriel was sent to Mary, a Virgin espoused to Joseph, to bring unto her the word of the Lord, and when the Virgin saw the light, she was afraid. Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace from the Lord.
responsory.repeat: Behold, thou shalt conceive and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

responsory.text: The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.
Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

verses.text: Audíte verbum Dómini príncipes Sodomórum: percípite áuribus legem Dei nostri pópulus Gomórrhæ.
Quo mihi multitúdinem victimárum vestrárum? dicit Dóminus. Plenus sum: holocáusta aríetum, et ádipem píngujum, et sánguinem vitulórum, et agnórum, et hircórum nólui.

responsory.text: Ave, María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum:
responsory.repeat: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.

responsory.text: Quómodo fiet istud, quóniam virum non cognósco? Et respóndens Angelus, dixit ei.
Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.

verses.text: Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom, give ear to the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrha.
To what purpose do you offer me the multitude of your victims, saith the Lord? I am full, I desire not holocausts of rams, and fat of fatlings, and blood of calves, and lambs, and buck goats.

responsory.text: Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with thee;
responsory.repeat: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

responsory.text: How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the Angel answered and said unto her,
The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Leónis Papæ
parts.source: Sermo 8 de jejunio decimi mensis et eleemosynis
paragraphs: Cum de advéntu regni Dei, et de mundi fine ac témporum, discípulos suos Salvátor instrúeret, totámque Ecclésiam suam in Apóstolis erudíret: Cavéte, inquit, ne forte gravéntur corda vestra in crápula, et ebrietáte, et cogitatiónibus sæculáribus. Quod útique præcéptum, dilectíssimi, ad nos speciálius pertinére cognóscimus, quibus denuntiátus dies, etiámsi est occúltus, non dubitátur esse vicínus.

responsory.text: Salvatórem exspectámus, Dóminum Jesum Christum,
responsory.repeat: Qui reformábit corpus humilitátis nostræ configurátum córpori claritátis suæ.

responsory.text: Sóbrie, et juste, et pie vivámus in hoc sǽculo, exspectántes beátam spem, et advéntum glóriæ magni Dei.
Qui reformábit corpus humilitátis nostræ configurátum córpori claritátis suæ.

parts.title: From the Sermons of Pope St. Leo (the Great,)
parts.source: 8th on the December Fast, and almsgiving.
paragraphs: Our Saviour Himself instructed His disciples concerning the times and seasons of the coming of the Kingdom of God and the end of the world, and He hath given the same teaching to the Church by the mouth of His Apostles. In connection with this subject then, Our Lord biddeth us beware lest we let our hearts grow heavy through excess of meat and drink, and worldly thoughts. Dearly beloved brethren, we know how that this warning applieth particularly to us. We know that that day is coming, and though for a season we know not the very hour, yet this we know, that it is near.

responsory.text: We look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ;
responsory.repeat: Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto His glorious Body.

responsory.text: We should live soberly, and righteously, and godly in this present world, looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God.
Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto His glorious Body.

paragraphs: Ad cujus advéntum omnem hóminem cónvenit præparári: ne quem aut ventri déditum, aut curis sæculáribus invéniat implicátum. Quotidiáno enim, dilectíssimi, experiménto probátur, potus satietáte áciem mentis obtúndi, et cibórum nimietáte vigórem cordis hebetári; ita ut delectátio edéndi étiam córporum contrária sit salúti, nisi rátio temperántiæ obsístat illécebræ, et quod futúrum est óneri, súbtrahat voluptáti.

responsory.text: Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, et annuntiáte illud in fínibus terræ, et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt dícite:
responsory.repeat: Salvátor noster advéniet.

responsory.text: Annuntiáte, et audítum fácite: loquímini, et clamáte.
Salvátor noster advéniet.

paragraphs: Let every man then make himself ready against the coming of the Lord, so that He may not find him making his belly his god, or the world his chief care. Dearly beloved brethren, it is a matter of every day experience that fulness of drink dulleth the keenness of the mind, and that excess of eating unnerveth the strength of the will. The very stomach protesteth that gluttony doth harm to the bodily health, unless temperance get the better of desire, and the thought of the indigestion afterward check the indulgence of the moment.

responsory.text: Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, et annuntiáte illud in fínibus terræ, et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt dícite:
responsory.repeat: Salvátor noster advéniet.

responsory.text: Declare it and make it known, lift up your voice and cry aloud.
Salvátor noster advéniet.

paragraphs: Quamvis enim sine ánima nihil caro desíderet, et inde accípiat sensus, unde sumit et motus: ejúsdem tamen est ánimæ, quædam sibi súbditæ negáre substántiæ, et interióri judício ab inconveniéntibus exterióra frenáre: ut a corpóreis cupiditátibus sǽpius líbera, in aula mentis possit divínæ vacáre sapiéntiæ: ubi omni strépitu terrenárum silénte curárum, in meditatiónibus sanctis, et in delíciis lætétur ætérnis.

responsory.text: Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus, et vocábitur nomen ejus,
responsory.repeat: Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

responsory.text: Super sólium David, et super regnum ejus sedébit in ætérnum.
Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

paragraphs: The body without the soul hath no desires; its sensibility cometh from the same source as its movements. And it is the duty of a man with a reasonable soul to deny something to his lower nature and to keep back the outer man from things unseemly. Then will his soul, free from fleshly cravings, sit often at leisure in the palace of the mind, dwelling on the wisdom of God. There, when the roar and rattle of earthly cares are stilled, will she feed on holy thoughts and entertain herself with the expectation of the everlasting joy.

responsory.text: Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus, et vocábitur nomen ejus,
responsory.repeat: Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

responsory.text: He shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom for ever.
Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

paragraphs: Quod si in hac vita diffícile est continuári, potest tamen frequénter assúmi; ut sǽpius ac diútius spiritálibus pótius quam carnálibus occupémur. Et cum melióribus curis majóres impéndimus moras, ad incorruptíbiles divítias étiam temporáles tránseunt actiónes.

responsory.text: Obsecro, Dómine, mitte quem missúrus es: vide afflictiónem pópuli tui:
responsory.repeat: Sicut locútus es, veni, et líbera nos.

responsory.text: Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui, vísita nos in salutári tuo:
Sicut locútus es, veni, et líbera nos.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Sicut locútus es, veni, et líbera nos.

paragraphs: And, although this is difficult to maintain in this life, yet the attempt can frequently be renewed, in order that we may the oftener and longer be occupied with spiritual rather than fleshly cares; and by our spending ever greater portions of our time on higher cares, even our temporal actions may end in gaining the incorruptible riches.

responsory.text: O my Lord, send I pray thee, Him Whom Thou wilt send; see the affliction of thy people. As Thou hast promised, come;
responsory.repeat: And deliver us.

responsory.text: Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui, vísita nos in salutári tuo:
And deliver us.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And deliver us.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Erunt signa in sole, et luna, et stellis, et in terris pressúra géntium. Et réliqua.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ
paragraphs: Dóminus ac Redémptor noster parátos nos inveníre desíderans, senescéntem mundum quæ mala sequántur denúntiat, ut nos ab ejus amóre compéscat. Appropinquántem ejus términum quantæ percussiónes prævéniant, innotéscit: ut, si Deum metúere in tranquillitáte nólumus, saltem vicínum ejus judícium vel percussiónibus attríti timeámus.

responsory.text: Læténtur cæli, et exsúltet terra, jubiláte, montes, laudem: quia Dóminus noster véniet,
responsory.repeat: Et páuperum suórum miserébitur.

responsory.text: Ecce dominátor Dóminus cum virtúte véniet.
Et páuperum suórum miserébitur.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Luke
paragraphs: In that time, Jesus said to his disciples: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations. And so on.

parts.title: Homily by Pope St. Gregory (the Great,)
paragraphs: Our Lord and Saviour wisheth to find us ready at His second coming. Therefore He telleth us what will be the evils of the world as it groweth old, that He may wean our hearts from worldly affections. Here we read what great convulsions will go before the end, that, if we will not fear God in our prosperity, we may at least be scourged into fearing His judgment when it is at hand.

responsory.text: Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains, for our Lord will come;
responsory.repeat: And will have mercy on His afflicted.

responsory.text: Ecce dominátor Dóminus cum virtúte véniet.
And will have mercy upon His afflicted.

paragraphs: Huic étenim lectióni sancti Evangélii, quam modo vestra fratérnitas audívit, paulo supérius Dóminus præmísit, dicens: Exsúrget gens contra gentem, et regnum advérsus regnum: et erunt terræmótus magni per loca, et pestiléntiæ, et fames. Et quibúsdam interpósitis, hoc, quod modo audístis, adjúnxit: Erunt signa in sole, et luna, et stellis, et in terris pressúra géntium præ confusióne sónitus maris, et flúctuum. Ex quibus profécto ómnibus ália jam facta cérnimus, ália in próximo ventúra formidámus.

responsory.text: Aliéni non transíbunt per Jerúsalem ámplius:
responsory.repeat: Nam in illa die stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, dicit Dóminus.

responsory.text: Ego véniam, dicit Dóminus, et sanábo contritiónem pópuli mei.
Nam in illa die stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, dicit Dóminus.

paragraphs: Immediately before the passage which hath just been read from the Gospel, are found the following words of our Lord, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and great earthquakes shall be in diverse places, and pestilences and famines. Then, after a few more verses, cometh today's Gospel. There shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations with perplexity, the sea and the waves roaring. Now some of these things are come to pass already, and we fear the others are not far off.

responsory.text: There shall no strangers pass through Jerusalem any more
responsory.repeat: For in that day the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey, saith the Lord.

responsory.text: Ego véniam, dicit Dóminus, et sanábo contritiónem pópuli mei.
For in that day the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey, saith the Lord.

paragraphs: Nam gentem contra gentem exsúrgere, earúmque pressúram terris insístere, plus jam in nostris tempóribus cérnimus, quam in codícibus légimus. Quod terræmótus urbes innúmeras óbruat, ex áliis mundi pártibus scitis quam frequénter audívimus. Pestiléntias sine cessatióne pátimur. Signa vero in sole, et luna, et stellis, adhuc apérte mínime vídimus: sed quia et hæc non longe sint, ex ipsa jam áëris immutatióne collígimus.

responsory.text: Montes Israël, ramos vestros expándite, et floréte, et fructus fácite:
responsory.repeat: Prope est ut véniat dies Dómini.

responsory.text: Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum: aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.
Prope est ut véniat dies Dómini.

paragraphs: In these our days we see nation rise against nation, and their distress over all the earth, more than we read in books hath ever come to pass of old time. Ye know also how often we hear of earthquakes overwhelming countless cities in other parts of the world. As for pestilences, we suffer from them ourselves, with hardly any intermission. As yet we do not see signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; but the changes of seasons and climates warn us that we may look for these also before long.

responsory.text: O ye mountains of Israel, shoot forth your branches and blossom and bring forth fruit.
responsory.repeat: The day of the Lord is at hand to come.

responsory.text: Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down the Righteous One; let the earth open, and let her bring forth the Saviour.
The day of the Lord is at hand to come.

paragraphs: Confúsio autem maris et flúctuum necdum nova exórta est. Sed cum multa prænuntiáta jam compléta sint, dúbium non est quin sequántur étiam pauca, quæ restant: quia sequéntium rerum certitúdo est præteritárum exhibítio.

responsory.text: Confortámini manus fatigátæ, et génua dissolúta roborámini: qui pusíllo ánimo estis mente convaléscite, me timéte, dicit Dóminus, quia vénio,
responsory.repeat: Dirúmpere jugum captivitátis vestræ.

responsory.text: Cívitas Jerúsalem, noli flere, qui cito véniet salus tua.
Dirúmpere jugum captivitátis vestræ.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Dirúmpere jugum captivitátis vestræ.

email.preheader: The vision of Isaias the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Juda and Jerusalem in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings o…
email.html:
The vision of Isaias the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Juda and Jerusalem in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings o…

Matins · Sunday, 29 November 2026

First Sunday of Advent

Dominica I Adventus · Semiduplex I classis

Commemorations: Vigil of St. Andrew the Apostle; St. Saturninus, Martyr

Read in Latin and English

Lesson I

Lesson from the book of Isaias

Isa 1:1-3

The vision of Isaias the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Juda and Jerusalem in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda Hear, O ye heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord hath spoken. I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me. The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel hath not known me, and my people hath not understood.

℟. I look from afar, and behold I see the Power of God, coming like as a cloud to cover the land with the hosts of his People: * Go ye out to meet him and say: * Tell us if thou art he, * That shalt reign over God's people Israel.

℣. All ye that dwell in the world, all ye children of men, high and low, rich and poor, one with another. Go ye out to meet him and say.

℣. Hear, O thou Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep. Tell us if thou art he.

℣. Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut salvos fácias nos. * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

Lesson II

Isa 1:4-6

Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a wicked seed, ungracious children: they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backwards. For what shall I strike you any more, you that increase transgression? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart is sad. From the sole of the foot unto the top of the head, there is no soundness therein: wounds and bruises and swelling sores: they are not bound up, nor dressed, nor fomented with oil.

℟. I saw in the night visions, and, behold, the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and there was given Him a Kingdom, and glory; * And all people, nations, and languages shall serve Him.

℣. His dominion is an everlasting dominion which shall not pass away, and His Kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.

℟. And all people, nations, and languages shall serve Him.

Lesson III

Isa 1:7-9

Your land is desolate, your cities are burnt with fire: your country strangers devour before your face, and it shall be desolate as when wasted by enemies. And the daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard, and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, and as a city that is laid waste. Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom, and we should have been like to Gomorrha.

℟. The Angel Gabriel was sent to Mary, a Virgin espoused to Joseph, to bring unto her the word of the Lord, and when the Virgin saw the light, she was afraid. Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace from the Lord. * Behold, thou shalt conceive and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

℣. The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.

℟. Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

Lesson IV

Isa 1:10-11

Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom, give ear to the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrha. To what purpose do you offer me the multitude of your victims, saith the Lord? I am full, I desire not holocausts of rams, and fat of fatlings, and blood of calves, and lambs, and buck goats.

℟. Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with thee; * The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

℣. How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the Angel answered and said unto her,

℟. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

Lesson V

From the Sermons of Pope St. Leo (the Great,)

8th on the December Fast, and almsgiving.

Our Saviour Himself instructed His disciples concerning the times and seasons of the coming of the Kingdom of God and the end of the world, and He hath given the same teaching to the Church by the mouth of His Apostles. In connection with this subject then, Our Lord biddeth us beware lest we let our hearts grow heavy through excess of meat and drink, and worldly thoughts. Dearly beloved brethren, we know how that this warning applieth particularly to us. We know that that day is coming, and though for a season we know not the very hour, yet this we know, that it is near.

℟. We look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ; * Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto His glorious Body.

℣. We should live soberly, and righteously, and godly in this present world, looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God.

℟. Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto His glorious Body.

Lesson VI

Let every man then make himself ready against the coming of the Lord, so that He may not find him making his belly his god, or the world his chief care. Dearly beloved brethren, it is a matter of every day experience that fulness of drink dulleth the keenness of the mind, and that excess of eating unnerveth the strength of the will. The very stomach protesteth that gluttony doth harm to the bodily health, unless temperance get the better of desire, and the thought of the indigestion afterward check the indulgence of the moment.

℟. Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, et annuntiáte illud in fínibus terræ, et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt dícite: * Salvátor noster advéniet.

℣. Declare it and make it known, lift up your voice and cry aloud.

℟. Salvátor noster advéniet.

Lesson VII

The body without the soul hath no desires; its sensibility cometh from the same source as its movements. And it is the duty of a man with a reasonable soul to deny something to his lower nature and to keep back the outer man from things unseemly. Then will his soul, free from fleshly cravings, sit often at leisure in the palace of the mind, dwelling on the wisdom of God. There, when the roar and rattle of earthly cares are stilled, will she feed on holy thoughts and entertain herself with the expectation of the everlasting joy.

℟. Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus, et vocábitur nomen ejus, * Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

℣. He shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom for ever.

℟. Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

Lesson VIII

And, although this is difficult to maintain in this life, yet the attempt can frequently be renewed, in order that we may the oftener and longer be occupied with spiritual rather than fleshly cares; and by our spending ever greater portions of our time on higher cares, even our temporal actions may end in gaining the incorruptible riches.

℟. O my Lord, send I pray thee, Him Whom Thou wilt send; see the affliction of thy people. As Thou hast promised, come; * And deliver us.

℣. Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui, vísita nos in salutári tuo:

℟. And deliver us.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And deliver us.

Lesson IX

From the Holy Gospel according to Luke

Luke 21:25-33

In that time, Jesus said to his disciples: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations. And so on.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory (the Great,)

1st on the Gospels

Our Lord and Saviour wisheth to find us ready at His second coming. Therefore He telleth us what will be the evils of the world as it groweth old, that He may wean our hearts from worldly affections. Here we read what great convulsions will go before the end, that, if we will not fear God in our prosperity, we may at least be scourged into fearing His judgment when it is at hand.

℟. Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains, for our Lord will come; * And will have mercy on His afflicted.

℣. Ecce dominátor Dóminus cum virtúte véniet.

℟. And will have mercy upon His afflicted.

Lesson X

Immediately before the passage which hath just been read from the Gospel, are found the following words of our Lord, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and great earthquakes shall be in diverse places, and pestilences and famines. Then, after a few more verses, cometh today's Gospel. There shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations with perplexity, the sea and the waves roaring. Now some of these things are come to pass already, and we fear the others are not far off.

℟. There shall no strangers pass through Jerusalem any more * For in that day the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey, saith the Lord.

℣. Ego véniam, dicit Dóminus, et sanábo contritiónem pópuli mei.

℟. For in that day the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey, saith the Lord.

Lesson XI

In these our days we see nation rise against nation, and their distress over all the earth, more than we read in books hath ever come to pass of old time. Ye know also how often we hear of earthquakes overwhelming countless cities in other parts of the world. As for pestilences, we suffer from them ourselves, with hardly any intermission. As yet we do not see signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; but the changes of seasons and climates warn us that we may look for these also before long.

℟. O ye mountains of Israel, shoot forth your branches and blossom and bring forth fruit. * The day of the Lord is at hand to come.

℣. Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down the Righteous One; let the earth open, and let her bring forth the Saviour.

℟. The day of the Lord is at hand to come.

Lesson XII

Confúsio autem maris et flúctuum necdum nova exórta est. Sed cum multa prænuntiáta jam compléta sint, dúbium non est quin sequántur étiam pauca, quæ restant: quia sequéntium rerum certitúdo est præteritárum exhibítio.

℟. Confortámini manus fatigátæ, et génua dissolúta roborámini: qui pusíllo ánimo estis mente convaléscite, me timéte, dicit Dóminus, quia vénio, * Dirúmpere jugum captivitátis vestræ.

℣. Cívitas Jerúsalem, noli flere, qui cito véniet salus tua.

℟. Dirúmpere jugum captivitátis vestræ.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Dirúmpere jugum captivitátis vestræ.

Te Deum

Read in Latin and English

Cistercian Breviary (Hohenfurth / Vyšší Brod). Texts from Divinum Officium (divinumofficium.com).

page.html:
Sunday, 29 November 2026

Dominica I AdventusFirst Sunday of Advent

Semiduplex I classis

Commemorationes: In Vigilia S. Andreæ Apostoli; S. Saturnini Martyris

Commemorations: Vigil of St. Andrew the Apostle; St. Saturninus, Martyr

Lectio I

Lesson I

Incipit liber Isaíæ Prophétæ

Lesson from the book of Isaias

Isa 1:1-3

Isa 1:1-3

Vísio Isaíæ fílii Amos, quam vidit super Judam et Jerúsalem, in diébus Ozíæ, Jóatham, Achaz, et Ezechíæ, regum Juda. Audíte, cæli, et áuribus pércipe, terra, quóniam Dóminus locútus est: Fílios enutrívi, et exaltávi: ipsi autem sprevérunt me. Cognóvit bos possessórem suum, et ásinus præsépe dómini sui: Israël autem me non cognóvit, et pópulus meus non intelléxit.

The vision of Isaias the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Juda and Jerusalem in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda Hear, O ye heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord hath spoken. I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me. The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel hath not known me, and my people hath not understood.

℟. Aspíciens a longe, ecce vídeo Dei poténtiam veniéntem, et nébulam totam terram tegéntem. * Ite óbviam ei, et dícite: * Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse, * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

℟. I look from afar, and behold I see the Power of God, coming like as a cloud to cover the land with the hosts of his People: * Go ye out to meet him and say: * Tell us if thou art he, * That shalt reign over God's people Israel.

℣. Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum, simul in unum dives et pauper. Ite óbviam ei, et dícite.

℣. All ye that dwell in the world, all ye children of men, high and low, rich and poor, one with another. Go ye out to meet him and say.

℣. Qui regis Israël, inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph. Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse.

℣. Hear, O thou Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep. Tell us if thou art he.

℣. Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut salvos fácias nos. * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

℣. Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut salvos fácias nos. * Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

Lectio II

Lesson II

Isa 1:4-6

Isa 1:4-6

Væ genti peccatríci, pópulo gravi iniquitáte, sémini nequam, fíliis scelerátis: dereliquérunt Dóminum, blasphemavérunt Sanctum Israël, abalienáti sunt retrórsum. Super quo percútiam vos ultra, addéntes prævaricatiónem? omne caput lánguidum, et omne cor mærens. A planta pedis usque ad vérticem non est in eo sánitas: vulnus, et livor, et plaga tumens non est circumligáta, nec curáta medicámine, neque fota óleo.

Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a wicked seed, ungracious children: they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backwards. For what shall I strike you any more, you that increase transgression? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart is sad. From the sole of the foot unto the top of the head, there is no soundness therein: wounds and bruises and swelling sores: they are not bound up, nor dressed, nor fomented with oil.

℟. Aspiciébam in visu noctis, et ecce in núbibus cæli Fílius hóminis veniébat: et datum est ei regnum, et honor: * Et omnis pópulus, tribus, et linguæ sérvient ei.

℟. I saw in the night visions, and, behold, the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and there was given Him a Kingdom, and glory; * And all people, nations, and languages shall serve Him.

℣. Potéstas ejus, potéstas ætérna, quæ non auferétur: et regnum ejus, quod non corrumpétur.

℣. His dominion is an everlasting dominion which shall not pass away, and His Kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.

℟. Et omnis pópulus, tribus, et linguæ sérvient ei.

℟. And all people, nations, and languages shall serve Him.

Lectio III

Lesson III

Isa 1:7-9

Isa 1:7-9

Terra vestra desérta, civitátes vestræ succénsæ igni: regiónem vestram coram vobis aliéni dévorant, et desolábitur sicut in vastitáte hostíli. Et derelinquétur fília Sion ut umbráculum in vínea, et sicut tugúrium in cucumerário, et sicut cívitas quæ vastátur. Nisi Dóminus exercítuum reliquísset nobis semen, quasi Sódoma fuissémus, et quasi Gomórrha símiles essémus.

Your land is desolate, your cities are burnt with fire: your country strangers devour before your face, and it shall be desolate as when wasted by enemies. And the daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard, and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, and as a city that is laid waste. Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom, and we should have been like to Gomorrha.

℟. Missus est Gábriel Angelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Joseph, núntians ei verbum; et expavéscit Virgo de lúmine: ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Dóminum: * Ecce concípies, et páries, et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.

℟. The Angel Gabriel was sent to Mary, a Virgin espoused to Joseph, to bring unto her the word of the Lord, and when the Virgin saw the light, she was afraid. Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace from the Lord. * Behold, thou shalt conceive and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

℣. Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris ejus, et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum.

℣. The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.

℟. Ecce concípies, et páries, et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.

℟. Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bring forth a son, and He shall be called the Son of the Highest.

Lectio IV

Lesson IV

Isa 1:10-11

Isa 1:10-11

Audíte verbum Dómini príncipes Sodomórum: percípite áuribus legem Dei nostri pópulus Gomórrhæ. Quo mihi multitúdinem victimárum vestrárum? dicit Dóminus. Plenus sum: holocáusta aríetum, et ádipem píngujum, et sánguinem vitulórum, et agnórum, et hircórum nólui.

Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom, give ear to the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrha. To what purpose do you offer me the multitude of your victims, saith the Lord? I am full, I desire not holocausts of rams, and fat of fatlings, and blood of calves, and lambs, and buck goats.

℟. Ave, María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum: * Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.

℟. Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with thee; * The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

℣. Quómodo fiet istud, quóniam virum non cognósco? Et respóndens Angelus, dixit ei.

℣. How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the Angel answered and said unto her,

℟. Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.

℟. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.

℟. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.

Lectio V

Lesson V

Sermo sancti Leónis Papæ

From the Sermons of Pope St. Leo (the Great,)

Sermo 8 de jejunio decimi mensis et eleemosynis

8th on the December Fast, and almsgiving.

Cum de advéntu regni Dei, et de mundi fine ac témporum, discípulos suos Salvátor instrúeret, totámque Ecclésiam suam in Apóstolis erudíret: Cavéte, inquit, ne forte gravéntur corda vestra in crápula, et ebrietáte, et cogitatiónibus sæculáribus. Quod útique præcéptum, dilectíssimi, ad nos speciálius pertinére cognóscimus, quibus denuntiátus dies, etiámsi est occúltus, non dubitátur esse vicínus.

Our Saviour Himself instructed His disciples concerning the times and seasons of the coming of the Kingdom of God and the end of the world, and He hath given the same teaching to the Church by the mouth of His Apostles. In connection with this subject then, Our Lord biddeth us beware lest we let our hearts grow heavy through excess of meat and drink, and worldly thoughts. Dearly beloved brethren, we know how that this warning applieth particularly to us. We know that that day is coming, and though for a season we know not the very hour, yet this we know, that it is near.

℟. Salvatórem exspectámus, Dóminum Jesum Christum, * Qui reformábit corpus humilitátis nostræ configurátum córpori claritátis suæ.

℟. We look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ; * Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto His glorious Body.

℣. Sóbrie, et juste, et pie vivámus in hoc sǽculo, exspectántes beátam spem, et advéntum glóriæ magni Dei.

℣. We should live soberly, and righteously, and godly in this present world, looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God.

℟. Qui reformábit corpus humilitátis nostræ configurátum córpori claritátis suæ.

℟. Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto His glorious Body.

Lectio VI

Lesson VI

Ad cujus advéntum omnem hóminem cónvenit præparári: ne quem aut ventri déditum, aut curis sæculáribus invéniat implicátum. Quotidiáno enim, dilectíssimi, experiménto probátur, potus satietáte áciem mentis obtúndi, et cibórum nimietáte vigórem cordis hebetári; ita ut delectátio edéndi étiam córporum contrária sit salúti, nisi rátio temperántiæ obsístat illécebræ, et quod futúrum est óneri, súbtrahat voluptáti.

Let every man then make himself ready against the coming of the Lord, so that He may not find him making his belly his god, or the world his chief care. Dearly beloved brethren, it is a matter of every day experience that fulness of drink dulleth the keenness of the mind, and that excess of eating unnerveth the strength of the will. The very stomach protesteth that gluttony doth harm to the bodily health, unless temperance get the better of desire, and the thought of the indigestion afterward check the indulgence of the moment.

℟. Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, et annuntiáte illud in fínibus terræ, et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt dícite: * Salvátor noster advéniet.

Lectio VII

Lesson VII

Quamvis enim sine ánima nihil caro desíderet, et inde accípiat sensus, unde sumit et motus: ejúsdem tamen est ánimæ, quædam sibi súbditæ negáre substántiæ, et interióri judício ab inconveniéntibus exterióra frenáre: ut a corpóreis cupiditátibus sǽpius líbera, in aula mentis possit divínæ vacáre sapiéntiæ: ubi omni strépitu terrenárum silénte curárum, in meditatiónibus sanctis, et in delíciis lætétur ætérnis.

The body without the soul hath no desires; its sensibility cometh from the same source as its movements. And it is the duty of a man with a reasonable soul to deny something to his lower nature and to keep back the outer man from things unseemly. Then will his soul, free from fleshly cravings, sit often at leisure in the palace of the mind, dwelling on the wisdom of God. There, when the roar and rattle of earthly cares are stilled, will she feed on holy thoughts and entertain herself with the expectation of the everlasting joy.

℟. Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus, et vocábitur nomen ejus, * Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

℟. Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus, et vocábitur nomen ejus, * Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

Lectio VIII

Lesson VIII

Quod si in hac vita diffícile est continuári, potest tamen frequénter assúmi; ut sǽpius ac diútius spiritálibus pótius quam carnálibus occupémur. Et cum melióribus curis majóres impéndimus moras, ad incorruptíbiles divítias étiam temporáles tránseunt actiónes.

And, although this is difficult to maintain in this life, yet the attempt can frequently be renewed, in order that we may the oftener and longer be occupied with spiritual rather than fleshly cares; and by our spending ever greater portions of our time on higher cares, even our temporal actions may end in gaining the incorruptible riches.

℟. Obsecro, Dómine, mitte quem missúrus es: vide afflictiónem pópuli tui: * Sicut locútus es, veni, et líbera nos.

℟. O my Lord, send I pray thee, Him Whom Thou wilt send; see the affliction of thy people. As Thou hast promised, come; * And deliver us.

Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ

Homily by Pope St. Gregory (the Great,)

Homilia 1 in Evangelia

1st on the Gospels

Dóminus ac Redémptor noster parátos nos inveníre desíderans, senescéntem mundum quæ mala sequántur denúntiat, ut nos ab ejus amóre compéscat. Appropinquántem ejus términum quantæ percussiónes prævéniant, innotéscit: ut, si Deum metúere in tranquillitáte nólumus, saltem vicínum ejus judícium vel percussiónibus attríti timeámus.

Our Lord and Saviour wisheth to find us ready at His second coming. Therefore He telleth us what will be the evils of the world as it groweth old, that He may wean our hearts from worldly affections. Here we read what great convulsions will go before the end, that, if we will not fear God in our prosperity, we may at least be scourged into fearing His judgment when it is at hand.

Lectio X

Lesson X

Huic étenim lectióni sancti Evangélii, quam modo vestra fratérnitas audívit, paulo supérius Dóminus præmísit, dicens: Exsúrget gens contra gentem, et regnum advérsus regnum: et erunt terræmótus magni per loca, et pestiléntiæ, et fames. Et quibúsdam interpósitis, hoc, quod modo audístis, adjúnxit: Erunt signa in sole, et luna, et stellis, et in terris pressúra géntium præ confusióne sónitus maris, et flúctuum. Ex quibus profécto ómnibus ália jam facta cérnimus, ália in próximo ventúra formidámus.

Immediately before the passage which hath just been read from the Gospel, are found the following words of our Lord, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and great earthquakes shall be in diverse places, and pestilences and famines. Then, after a few more verses, cometh today's Gospel. There shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations with perplexity, the sea and the waves roaring. Now some of these things are come to pass already, and we fear the others are not far off.

℟. Aliéni non transíbunt per Jerúsalem ámplius: * Nam in illa die stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, dicit Dóminus.

℟. There shall no strangers pass through Jerusalem any more * For in that day the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey, saith the Lord.

℣. Ego véniam, dicit Dóminus, et sanábo contritiónem pópuli mei.

Lectio XI

Lesson XI

Nam gentem contra gentem exsúrgere, earúmque pressúram terris insístere, plus jam in nostris tempóribus cérnimus, quam in codícibus légimus. Quod terræmótus urbes innúmeras óbruat, ex áliis mundi pártibus scitis quam frequénter audívimus. Pestiléntias sine cessatióne pátimur. Signa vero in sole, et luna, et stellis, adhuc apérte mínime vídimus: sed quia et hæc non longe sint, ex ipsa jam áëris immutatióne collígimus.

In these our days we see nation rise against nation, and their distress over all the earth, more than we read in books hath ever come to pass of old time. Ye know also how often we hear of earthquakes overwhelming countless cities in other parts of the world. As for pestilences, we suffer from them ourselves, with hardly any intermission. As yet we do not see signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; but the changes of seasons and climates warn us that we may look for these also before long.

℟. Montes Israël, ramos vestros expándite, et floréte, et fructus fácite: * Prope est ut véniat dies Dómini.

℟. O ye mountains of Israel, shoot forth your branches and blossom and bring forth fruit. * The day of the Lord is at hand to come.

℣. Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum: aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.

℣. Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down the Righteous One; let the earth open, and let her bring forth the Saviour.

℟. Prope est ut véniat dies Dómini.

℟. The day of the Lord is at hand to come.
